papers.title: A Large Gap between Galerkin Errors with and without Mesh-Uniform Regularity for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
papers.abstract: We compare two cubic Hermite Galerkin semidiscretizations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. They use the same trial space. The first is the weighted scheme considered in our previous paper (arXiv:2610.39269), called the W-scheme. It has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. The second is the standard Galerkin method in $L^2$, called the S-scheme. It has no mesh-uniform regularity. For the W-scheme, the full error and the ordering error converge at an algebraic rate in $h$, uniformly on $[t_0,\infty)$ times small balls of $L^2$ for any fixed $t_0>0$. They are bounded by $Ch^p\varepsilon$ and $Ch^p\varepsilon^2$, respectively, where $\varepsilon$ is the size of the datum and $p>0$. We prove that neither bound holds for the S-scheme by using exact high-frequency spurious eigenpairs of the S-scheme. The existence of such eigenpairs for fine meshes with at least 512 elements has a proof checked by Lean 4. Computations compare the two schemes on unit-norm data built from these eigenfunctions, on 512, 1024 and 2048 elements. The full error of the S-scheme stays at $4.6\times10^{-2}$. That of the W-scheme is at most $2.2\times10^{-9}$. The ordering error of the S-scheme stays at $9.6\times10^{-6}$. That of the W-scheme falls from $2.3\times10^{-9}$ to $1.4\times10^{-10}$. Their ratio grows from $4.2\times10^3$ to $6.6\times10^4$.

papers.title: Deep backward multistep high-order regression methods for high dimensional nonlinear parabolic partial differential equations
papers.abstract: We propose a deep backward multistep high-order regression (MHDBR) method for semilinear parabolic partial differential equations through their backward stochastic differential equation representations. The method combines multistep time discretization with regression targets formed by conditional expectations. Under explicit regularity, starting-value, forward-approximation and network-moment assumptions, we prove an error bound separating time discretization, conditional Monte Carlo sampling and neural-network approximation. The analysis assumes exact population minimization; finite-training-sample generalization and optimization errors are not included. For generators independent of the gradient variable, suitably constrained GroupSort networks and sufficiently large conditional sample sizes give order $J$ in the stated nodal $L^2$ error norm. The required network sizes depend on dimension, so this result does not establish dimension-independent complexity. We present a reproducible time-discretization test satisfying the analytical assumptions and three broader neural-network benchmarks, whose relation to the assumptions is discussed explicitly.

papers.title: Uniform Exponential Stability Analysis of Impulsive Linear Time-Invariant Systems on Banach and Hilbert Spaces: Non-Coercive and Coercive Stability Conditions
papers.abstract: We consider the uniform exponential stability analysis of infinite-dimensional impulsive systems defined on a Banach or Hilbert space, whose flow is governed by a fixed $C_0$-semigroup generator and whose jumps occur at a prescribed time sequence. While the flow and jump maps are themselves time-invariant, the time-triggered impulses render the propagator a genuinely time-varying evolution family, which is the source of the analysis difficulty addressed here. We combine ideas from hybrid systems theory and infinite-dimensional systems to produce operator-based stability conditions, which can be analytically or numerically checked via convex programming. Necessary and sufficient conditions for the uniform exponential stability of impulsive systems on Banach spaces are obtained in the context of a fixed impulse-times sequence but also of arbitrary, constant, minimum, and range dwell-times using both non-coercive and coercive Lyapunov functionals. Some of those results are then adapted to systems on a Hilbert space and quadratic Lyapunov functionals. As an application, linear switched systems are shown to be an exact special case: reformulated as impulsive systems with unit-norm selector jumps, they inherit non-coercive and clock-dependent dwell-time stability conditions on both Banach and Hilbert spaces. Theoretical and numerical examples are given for illustration, notably on the sampled-data control of time-delay systems.

papers.title: Non-Uniqueness of Weak Solutions to the Unforced Two-Dimensional Euler Equations with Vorticity in $L^1\cap L^p$, Part II: The Nonlinear Construction
papers.abstract: This paper and its companion Part I prove that the incompressible Euler equations in the plane, without external force, admit two distinct renormalized weak solutions with the same initial vorticity $f$, where $f$ is radial and nonnegative and lies in $(L^1\cap L^q)(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for every $q<\infty$ but is not bounded. One solution is radially symmetric and stationary. The other is $3$-fold rotationally symmetric, is equimeasurable with $f$ at every time, and departs from $f$ in finite time; the two solutions are distinct in $L^\infty_t(L^1\cap L^q)_x$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^2$ for every $q\in(4/3,\infty)$ and every sufficiently large $T$. The nonstationary solution belongs to $C([0,\infty);L^q(\mathbb{R}^2))$ for every $q\in[1,\infty)$. Part I establishes a compactness criterion for non-uniqueness and conditional linear instability results for a vortex ring. Part II establishes the hypotheses of those results and proves the nonlinear non-uniqueness theorem.

papers.title: The Whitney Extension Problem in Carnot groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a Carnot group, let $E \subset \mathbb{G}$ be compact, and suppose we are given a function $f: E \to \mathbb{R}$. The $C^1_H$ {\em Whitney Extension Problem} asks the following: what must be true about $f$ to guarantee that there exists a smooth, horizontal function $F \in C^1_H(\mathbb{G})$ extending $f$, i.e., there is some $F:\mathbb{G} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $F|_E = f|_E$ and $XF$ is continuous for every horizontal left invariant vector field $X$? We adapt the method of G. Glaeser and C. Fefferman to answer this question in this non-commutative setting. Moreover, we provide an alternative solution to the $C^1$ Whitney Extension Problem for horizontal curves in the Heisenberg group.

papers.title: Stability in the Non-Neutral and Neutral Regimes of the Holonomy-Based Inverse Problem in the Class \(\mathcal{OC}\)
papers.abstract: We study anchor reconstruction stability in return-map inverse problems for class $\mathcal O_C$. Local identifiability is governed by the first nonvanishing derivative of the holonomy map $H = T_\gamma - \text{Id}$. In the non-neutral case, we prove local Lipschitz stability and multiplier estimates. In the neutral regime, using Fa\`a di Bruno equations and Malgrange preparation, we derive quantitative $1/k$-H\"older estimates for order-$k$ anchor perturbations. We also establish finite jet stability, real-analytic dependence, and global $C^0$-stability of order $O(\varepsilon_F^{1/k})$. Numerical benchmarks on circular-core return geometries validate these theoretical convergence rates and square-root laws.

papers.title: On the V\'azquez Strong Maximum Principle for Linear and Nonlinear Elliptic Equations with Unbounded Coefficients and Optimal Conditions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present adaptations of the classical strong maximum principle for a certain class of equations, with particular emphasis on linear operators in non-divergence form and a new strategy to prove it. The novelty of our approach lies in the setting of the problem: the coefficients of the operators are unbounded, assumed to be merely integrable in the $L^{p,q}$-sense, and the source term $f$ on the right-hand side of the equation is treated under optimal integrability assumptions.

papers.title: V\'azquez Strong Maximum Principle and Compact Support Principle for singular and degenerate elliptical operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present adaptations of the classical strong maximum principle and the compact support principle for a certain class of equations, with particular emphasis on the degeneracy of fully nonlinear operators and a new V\'azquez-type condition on the nonhomogeneous term. The novelty of our approach lies in the framework of the problem: the coefficients of the operators are bounded, but we introduce a degeneracy depending on the power of the gradient of the solution. Moreover, the source term $f$ on the right-hand side of the equation is treated under a adapted and optimal integrability assumptions.

papers.title: Nonexistence of positive solutions stable outside a compact set for the Lane--Emden system in a half-space
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension and for all positive exponents, the Lane--Emden system in a half-space with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions admits no positive classical solution stable outside a compact set.

papers.title: Local regularity and p-harmonic approximation for weak inverse mean curvature flow
papers.abstract: We prove local Lipschitz regularity for locally bounded $BV$ solutions of the calibration equations for inverse mean curvature flow. We also approximate every prescribed variational weak flow locally by Moser's logarithmic transforms of positive $p$-harmonic functions. On a fixed smooth domain, with the trace of a calibrated Lipschitz solution prescribed, both the uniform error and the absolute difference of total variations are $O((p-1)^{1/3})$ as $p\downarrow1$. In particular, the approximations converge strictly in $BV$.

papers.title: Formal Proof of an Anisotropic Calder\'on Uniqueness Theorem
papers.abstract: We announce a Lean~4 formal proof of a special case of the smooth anisotropic Calder\'on uniqueness theorem released by OpenAI on October 6, 2026. We consider smooth Riemannian metrics on the three-dimensional unit ball, with full boundary measurements and Euclidean extensions outside the ball. OpenAI's release did not include a Lean proof of their uniqueness result. Our formalization uses results from Mathlib and Tau Ceti, and it is given as a solution to a Lean comparator challenge whose check permits only the standard axioms of Lean. The Lean proof is not a line-by-line translation of the OpenAI manuscript.

papers.title: On the domain of attraction of source--type solutions of the porous medium equations
papers.abstract: We study the rate of convergence to Barenblatt profiles of the solutions to porous medium equations in $\R^n, n \ge 1$, by means of a certain class of Energy distances, a class of discrepancies between probability measures which have been recently widely used in problems related to AI, in particular for tasks related to machine learning. If $n \ge 3$, it is shown both that the rate of decay in Energy distance is improved with respect to known results which are based on the decay of relative entropy, and that, with respect to this distance, any initial value of bounded mass belongs to the domain of attraction of the source--type solution. Similar results are shown to hold for the fast diffusion case.

papers.title: From many-body Schr\"odinger dynamics to magnetic Vlasov equation
papers.abstract: We analyse the combined mean-field and semiclassical limit from the time-dependent Schr\"odinger dynamics of $N$ spinless fermions in a non-constant magnetic field to the magnetic Vlasov equation with scaling $\hbar = N^{-1/3}$. With the velocity-shifted coherent states and the induced magnetic Husimi measure, we derive an exact BBGKY hierarchy with a remainder of order $\hbar^{1/2-}$. The main result is the weak $L^1$ convergence of the $k$-particle magnetic Husimi measures to the $k$-copies of the solution to the magnetic Vlasov equation. Furthermore, the convergence holds in the Wasserstein distance $\mathbb{W}_2$ when the second moment of initial Husimi measure correspondingly converges.

papers.title: Mean Field Limit Towards Kinetic Equation with Repulsive Dirac-Delta Potential
papers.abstract: A one-particle effective kinetic equation with repulsive Dirac-Delta potential in one dimension is rigorously derived from a moderate interacting second order particle system. It is proved that the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure and the solution of Vlasov equation converges to zero. A convergence rate is obtained by a combination of the estimates for particle trajectory and a smoothed version of modulated energy.

papers.title: Total Variation Regularized Barycenters in Wasserstein Space
papers.abstract: We study total variation regularization of Wasserstein barycenters on bounded connected Lipschitz domains. We prove existence for arbitrary prescribed probability measures and uniqueness when at least one is absolutely continuous. Our main results are attained dual formulations in terms of relative perimeters and vector fields with zero normal trace. These yield necessary and sufficient optimality conditions and a variational characterization of superlevel sets. We also establish a maximum principle on convex domains, stability of minimizers, and an exact reduction to a single TV-JKO step in one dimension. The existence, uniqueness, and perimeter duality results extend to costs $|x-y|^p$, $p>1$, under the same assumptions.

papers.title: Zero extension for the Dirichlet problem on graphs
papers.abstract: Solutions of the Dirichlet problem on a finite part of a weighted graph are extended by zero, together with their source, to a larger connected part. A necessary and sufficient condition is proved for the extended function to remain a solution of the corresponding Dirichlet problem on the enlarged domain: at every newly included vertex adjacent to the original part, the weighted sum of the solution over its neighbors in that part must vanish. The admissible sources are characterized as the orthogonal complement of the harmonic extensions from the enlarged domain to the original part, their space has dimension equal to the number of vertices of the original part minus the rank of the interface coupling, and an exact energy identity for the extension error follows from a Schur complement of the graph Laplacian. The same reduction covers other boundary conditions, including the Neumann problem, and extends to higher powers of the Laplacian, where the boundary data must be compatible with the lower-order interface traces. The discrete criterion is compared with its continuous counterpart, and no result in this form has been reported on Riemannian manifolds.

papers.title: Nonlinear stability and time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract: We prove the global-in-time nonlinear stability and establish explicit algebraic time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system of an ideal polytropic gas in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Given a smooth initial rarefaction profile of small wave strength \(\delta>0\), we first construct the corresponding global one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier solution \(U_b(t,x_1)\) and show that it converges toward the self-similar Euler rarefaction fan in \(L^\infty(\mathbb{R})\) at rate \((1+t)^{-12/25}\). For the three-dimensional Cauchy problem under small weighted $H^3(\mathbb{R}^3)$ perturbations with zero integral of mass, momentum, and total energy, we prove that there exists a unique global strong solution $U(t,x)$ converging toward $U_b(t,x_1)$ in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$, with $\nabla(U-U_b)$ decaying in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$.

papers.title: Embeddings for Orlicz potential spaces with applications to mixed local-nonlocal problems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide further insight into potential spaces within the nonstandard framework of Orlicz functions. More precisely, we establish continuous and compact embeddings of potential spaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$ into both unweighted and weighted Orlicz spaces. Special attention is devoted to the radial setting, for which compactness results are obtained through Strauss- and Ni-type inequalities. As an application, we prove the existence of positive radial solutions to a class of Henon-type problems involving both local and nonlocal contributions in the Orlicz framework.

papers.title: Local turnpike property for a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model
papers.abstract: We study a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model. It couples Hamilton--Jacobi and Fokker--Planck equations for the harvesters with a reaction-diffusion equation for the resource. The coupling is nonlocal in space and time. For standard second-order mean field game systems, exponential turnpike estimates are known under assumptions such as monotonicity of the coupling. For the present system, Kobeissi, Mazari-Fouquer, and Ruiz-Balet proved algebraic convergence to a stationary solution in a space--time averaged sense, but no exponential turnpike estimate has been obtained. We prove such an estimate near a stationary solution with strictly positive density components. Inspired by the relative entropy method, we add the relative entropy of the resource density to the standard energy for local turnpike estimates. In the time derivative of this modified energy, the nonlocal coupling terms cancel. The two key assumptions are coercivity of a quadratic form determined by the stationary resource density and smallness of the relative density perturbations in $L^\infty$. Under these assumptions, we bound the absolute value of the modified energy by two terms that decay exponentially away from the initial and terminal times. We derive weighted $L^2$ exponential turnpike estimates for the harvester density, the resource density, and the gradient of the value function. We give sufficient conditions for coercivity. For each fixed $T>0$, classical solutions satisfying these assumptions exist for initial and terminal data sufficiently close to the stationary solution. We extend the modified energy estimate to a more general reaction term under the corresponding assumptions.

papers.title: A sufficient condition for the Liouville property of solutions to the Euler-Lagrange equations of variational integrals with nonstandard growth in terms of the ellipticity modulus near the origin
papers.abstract: We consider entire solutions $u$: $\mathbb{R}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of the Euler-Lagrange equation $\operatorname{div}(\nabla f(\nabla u))=0$ with convex density $f$: $\mathbb{R}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of nonstandard growth and nonuniform ellipticity. It turns out that the Liouville property can be characterized through the behavior of $D^{2}f(p)$ for points $p\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ close to the origin: if, for example, $D^{2}f(p)$ behaves as $|p|^{\rho-2}\mathbf{1}$, $\mathbf{1}=\text{unit matrix}$, with exponent $\rho\ge2$ and for $|p|\le1$ then the validity of $n\le\rho+2$ together with the boundedness of $u$ implies its constancy.

papers.title: Propagation phenomena in spatial periodic bistable reaction-diffusion equations around an obstacle
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with propagation phenomena for a spatially periodic bistable reaction--diffusion equation around an obstacle. It is known that an entire solution emanating from a pulsating front converges to the same front as \(t\rightaroow+\infty\) under complete propagation and an additional technical assumption. We remove the technical assumption and prove that the entire solution coming from a pulsating front converges to the same pulsating front as \(t\rightarrow+\infty\) under the complete propagation.

papers.title: Superlinear problems related to Fully Non Linear singular or degenerate operators in punctured balls
papers.abstract: We study Fully Nonlinear uniformly elliptic equations with a higher differential term degenerate or singular, coupled with a zero order term singular at the point $0$, and an absorbing super-linear term of $p$ power type. We will limitate to punctured balls and positive radial solutions. In the continuity of two previous works in \cite {BDL1}, \cite{BDL2}, we will provide a complete classification depending on $p$ of the asymptotic behaviour of the solutions near the singular point $0$.

papers.title: Sharp Constants and Maximizers for Weighted Moser--Trudinger Inequalities on the Heisenberg Group
papers.abstract: This article concerns Moser-Trudinger inequalities on the entire Heisenberg group, focusing on sharp constants, maximizers, and applications to subelliptic PDEs. We address several questions on the existence of maximizers in the singular case $0<\beta<Q$, where the singular weight yields compactness. We first establish an Adimurthi-Druet-type weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality without blow-up analysis and determine its sharp constant. We also prove its equivalence with the critical weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality. For the subcritical inequality of Lam, Lu and Tang \cite{Lam-Lu-Tang-2014}, we obtain two-sided asymptotic bounds near the sharp threshold and prove existence of maximizers in a suitable regime. This inequality also yields insight into borderline Sobolev theory and an asymptotic Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg interpolation-type inequality. We further establish a weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality under inhomogeneous norm constraints and prove its equivalence with the subcritical inequality, thereby characterizing the associated supremum and its maximizers. An improved subcritical weighted inequality is also derived, and its maximization problem is shown to admit a maximizer. Finally, these inequalities are applied to normalized subelliptic equations driven by the $Q$-sub-Laplacian with nonlinearities having singular critical exponential growth at infinity. We prove the existence of nontrivial ground states for every prescribed mass $a>0$, provided the nonlinearity is sufficiently large in a suitable sense depending on $a$.

papers.title: Higher-order Sobolev stability and temporal decay estimate for the tropical climate model with small $H^1$ data
papers.abstract: We study the stability and temporal decay of solutions to the two-dimensional tropical climate model with Laplacian dissipation in both velocity equations and no thermal diffusion. For initial data in $H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ ($s \geq 1$) with sufficiently small $H^1$ norm, we establish a unique global solution satisfying uniform $H^s$ bounds and time-integrated estimates for the velocity and temperature. The smallness is independent of $s$, and the higher Sobolev norms of the initial data need not be small. Furthermore, without additional spatial integrability or negative-order regularity of the initial data, we prove that the $\dot H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ norms of the solutions are $o(t^{- s / 2})$ as $t \to \infty$. We also show that this decay rate is sharp: no additional decay factor tending to zero works for all such initial data.

papers.title: A uniform lower bound for logarithmic Trudinger-Moser suprema in dimension $N\ge3$
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be the unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge2$, and let $\mathrm{MT}_N(\alpha_{N,\beta},\beta)$ denote the critical Trudinger-Moser supremum of Calanchi and Ruf for radial functions in the Sobolev space with logarithmic weight $(-\log|x|)^{\beta(N-1)}$, $0\le\beta<1$. We prove that $\mathrm{MT}_N(\alpha_{N,\beta},\beta)>(2N-\frac25)|B|$ for every $\beta\in[0,1)$ and $N\ge 3$. This lower bound is uniform in $\beta$ and lies strictly above the upper bound $|B|\big(1+e^{1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1{N-1}}\big)$ for the concentration level obtained by Carleson-Chang for $\beta=0$ and, for $\beta>0$, by Roy for $N=2$ and by Roy and Nguyen for $N\ge 3$. As a consequence, we prove that $\mathrm{MT}_N(\alpha_{N,\beta},\beta)$ is attained for every $\beta\in[0,1)$ and $N\ge3$, which was previously known only for $\beta>0$ small enough. For $N=2$, the existence of extremals for every $\beta\in [0, 1)$ was recently obtained by de Oliveira.

papers.title: Almost sharp global well-posedness and low-regularity blow-up for the two-dimensional periodic Zakharov system
papers.abstract: We study the Zakharov system on an arbitrary fixed rectangular two-dimensional torus with initial data in $H^s\times L^2\times H^{-1}$. For the Schr\"odinger regularity $s$, Kishimoto proved local well-posedness for $1/2\leq s\leq1$ and global well-posedness for $9/14<s<1$ below the Euclidean cubic ground-state mass. Under the same mass condition, we prove global well-posedness for every $1/2<s<1$, with polynomial bounds for the Sobolev norms. We add quartic and quintic corrections to Kishimoto's resonantly modified energy. The main difficulty is to cancel the interactions obstructing the global iteration without introducing singular coefficients near resonance or losing control of the higher-order terms generated by differentiation. The coefficients exploit cancellations between successive nonlinear interactions. Away from resonance, they cancel the problematic terms; near resonance, algebraic rearrangements avoid division by small phases and preserve sufficient frequency decay. For every $s<1/2$, we also construct solutions with arbitrarily small initial data in $H^s\times L^2\times H^{-1}$ whose wave component blows up in finite time while the Schr\"odinger component remains bounded in $H^s$. We combine explicit approximate solutions supported on three Fourier modes with stability at $H^{1/2}\times L^2$. Choosing successively larger frequencies controls the nonlinear interactions among infinitely many approximate solutions and makes the accumulated errors summable, while their wave amplitudes produce blow-up. These results identify $s=1/2$ as the threshold between global well-posedness and the existence of such blow-up solutions, with the endpoint unresolved.

papers.title: Relative Entropy Methods for Rotating Stars in the Compressible Euler-Riesz Equations
papers.abstract: We establish finite-time relative entropy estimates for axisymmetric finite-energy entropy solutions of the three-dimensional attractive compressible Euler-Riesz equations near a prescribed compactly supported rotating star. The entropy solutions are assumed to have the same total mass as the steady state and to satisfy the prescribed angular momentum relation. For general pressure laws, the compatibility with the angular momentum constraint, together with the nonnegative rotational remainder, yields a cancellation of the centrifugal terms. For axisymmetric perturbations, the gradient of the perturbed Riesz potential has no azimuthal component and therefore couples only to those momentum components controlled by the modulated kinetic energy. The density-weighted estimates for the Riesz potential then allow us to close the relative entropy inequality. Under an additional higher-integrability assumption on the density, the result extends to the Chandrasekhar pressure law, yielding a corresponding stability estimate for rotating white dwarf stars.

papers.title: The sharp Fourier extension estimate for the sphere
papers.abstract: The full strong Fourier extension estimate for the unit sphere is established in every ambient dimension at least three. The finite Knapp boundary is obtained by combining a uniform diagonal estimate on rescaled spherical graphs with a transverse product bound. A Whitney decomposition and a dyadic dual pairing yield strong type at the exact scaling exponents. The critical local estimate and the strict mixed range come from the recent work on Euclidean local smoothing.

papers.title: Well-posedness and attractors for the sub-quintic weakly damped wave equation with low-regularity forcing on $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract: We study the weakly damped semilinear wave equation on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a sub-quintic nonlinearity $f(u)$ and a forcing term of low regularity, $g\in H^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^3)$. By absorbing the forcing term into a stationary solution $h$ and then expanding the solution around $h$, we reduce the problem to a wave equation with potentials. Relying on Strichartz estimates for this equation, obtained through the Besov spaces associated with the Schr\"odinger operator, we establish the global well-posedness of weak solutions by an iteration argument on the Besov scale. In particular, uniqueness holds unconditionally in the energy class for $3<p<5$. Combining a refined decomposition of the solution with uniform tail estimates for trajectories starting from bounded sets, we then prove that the associated solution semigroup is asymptotically compact and, consequently, possesses a compact global attractor in the energy space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)\times L^2(\mathbb{R}R^3)$.

papers.title: The Dirichlet problem for complex Monge--Amp\`ere equations with H\"older continuous right-hand sides
papers.abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation on bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains with $C^3$ boundary and $C^3$ boundary values. For every $n\ge2$ and $0<\alpha<1$, each continuous Bedford--Taylor solution with a strictly positive $C^\alpha$ right-hand side satisfies a global $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate. There is a unique such solution, which is strictly plurisubharmonic up to the boundary. Combining new boundary estimates with weighted integral estimates for the trace of the complex Hessian along an auxiliary parabolic flow, we obtain global $C^{1,\beta}$ bounds for every fixed $0<\beta<1$ in every dimension. Green function estimates and comparison arguments near the boundary give the boundary Hessian bound. Solutions of auxiliary Dirichlet problems with locally constant right-hand sides have uniform $W^{2,2n^2}$ bounds. Rescaling and interpolation then reduce the global Hessian estimate to interior regularity.
